title: Belief
sub: What every Muslim must believe about Allah and His Messengers ﷺ

cards.x: Every Muslim who has reached adulthood and is sane must know what is necessary for Allah, what is impossible for Him, and what is possible for Him. The same applies to the Messengers عليهم السلام.
Something is necessary if the mind cannot picture it not being there. It is impossible if the mind cannot picture it existing. It is possible if the mind can picture it existing or not existing.
Knowing these things protects your belief from doubt. You don't need to be a scholar: you need to know them clearly and be sure of them.

checks.q: Who must know what is necessary, impossible and possible for Allah?
Something the mind cannot picture not existing is called…
Something the mind can picture existing or not existing is called…

lessons.title: Allah exists, without beginning or end

cards.x: Allah exists. His existence has no cause and does not depend on anything.
Allah has no beginning (qidam). Everything else came into being after not existing; He did not.
Allah has no end (baqa'). He will never cease to be. As Imam al-Tahawi رحمه الله says: He is Eternal without a beginning and Everlasting without an end.

checks.q: What does it mean that Allah has no beginning?
checks.a: He never came into being; He always was
w: He was created before everything else
He began when the universe began
No one knows if He has a beginning

checks.q: What does it mean that Allah has no end?
checks.a: He will never cease to exist
w: He will end after the Last Day
He ends when the world ends

checks.q: Does Allah's existence depend on anything?

cards.x: Allah does not resemble anything He created. He is not a body, He is not in a place, and He is not bound by time. 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.' (al-Shura 11)
Allah stands by Himself (qiyam bi-nafsihi): He needs no place and no one to bring Him into being. Everything needs Him.
Allah is One (wahdaniyyah): One in His Self, One in His attributes and One in His actions. He has no partner and no equal.

checks.q: Which is true about Allah?
checks.a: He does not resemble anything He created
w: He has a body unlike ours
He is in one particular place
He is bound by time like us

checks.q: What does it mean that Allah 'stands by Himself'?
checks.a: He needs nothing, while everything needs Him
w: He needs His throne to exist

checks.q: Allah's Oneness covers…
checks.a: His Self, His attributes and His actions

cards.x: Allah has Power (qudrah) over every possible thing, and Will (iradah): nothing happens except what He wills.
Allah has Knowledge ('ilm) of everything: what was, what is, what will be, and what would be. He is Living (hayah) with a life unlike ours.
Allah hears (sam') and sees (basar) all that exists, without ears or eyes. He speaks (kalam) with an eternal speech that is not letters or sounds. The Qur'an is His speech.

checks.q: Nothing happens in creation except…
How does Allah hear and see?
checks.a: Without ears or eyes, unlike creation
w: With ears and eyes like ours
He does not hear or see

checks.q: Allah's speech is…
checks.a: Eternal, and not made of letters or sounds
w: Something that began with the Qur'an

cards.x: The Messengers are truthful (sidq), trustworthy (amanah) and convey everything they were commanded to convey (tabligh).
Lying, betraying trust, and hiding what they were commanded to convey are impossible for them.
Human things that do not lower their rank are possible for them, such as eating, sleeping, marriage and illness that is not repulsive.
Muhammad ﷺ is the last Prophet and the Messenger to all of mankind and jinn. There is no prophet after him.

checks.q: Which is necessary for every Messenger?
checks.a: Truthfulness, trustworthiness and conveying the message

checks.q: Which is possible for a Messenger?
Who is the last Prophet?
w: There will be another after him

cards.x: A believer believes in Allah, His angels, His books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and that good and bad are by Allah's decree.
Faith (iman) is affirming with the tongue and believing with the heart everything the Prophet ﷺ brought from Allah.
We love the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We do not go to excess in loving any one of them, and we do not disown any of them. We mention them only with good.

checks.q: According to al-Tahawi, faith is…
checks.a: Affirming with the tongue and believing with the heart
w: Only believing, with no need to say it
Only saying it with the tongue

checks.q: Which is one of the articles of faith?
checks.a: Belief in Allah's decree, the good and the bad
w: Belief that the stars decide events
Belief that some saints are prophets

checks.q: How do we speak of the Companions?
checks.a: Only with good, without going to excess about any of them
w: We praise some and disown others

cards.x: You may purify yourself with seven kinds of water: rain, sea, river, well, melted snow, melted hail and spring water.
If something pure is mixed with water and the water is still called water, you may use it. If it has become something else, like juice or soup, you may not.
Water that has already been used for wudu or ghusl is pure, but you cannot purify yourself with it again.

checks.q: Which water can be used for wudu?
Can you make wudu with water used for someone's ghusl?
checks.a: No: it is pure but does not purify

checks.q: How many kinds of water does Nur al-Idah list for purification?

cards.x: Wash the whole face: from the top of the forehead to under the chin, and from one earlobe to the other.
Wash both hands and arms, including the elbows.
Wipe at least a quarter of the head with a wet hand.
Wash both feet, including the ankles. If any of these four is missed, the wudu is not valid.

checks.q: How much of the head must be wiped in wudu?
How far must the arms be washed?
Which of these is one of the four obligations of wudu?
checks.a: Washing the feet including the ankles

cards.x: Have the intention, say bismillah, wash the hands to the wrists and use the siwak (even a finger if you have no siwak).
Rinse the mouth three times and sniff water into the nose three times.
Wash each part three times, wipe the whole head once and the ears, run water between the fingers and toes, start with the right, follow the order Allah mentions, and keep going without long breaks.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, rinsing the mouth in wudu is…
How many times is each part washed according to the sunnah?
Which is a sunnah of wudu?
w: Wiping the neck with the back of the hand only

cards.x: Anything that comes out of the front or back passage, flowing blood or pus, and vomit that fills the mouth all break wudu.
Sleeping without being seated firmly on the ground breaks it, as do fainting, insanity and drunkenness.
Laughing out loud in a prayer with bowing and prostration breaks both the prayer and the wudu, for a sane, awake adult.
Touching your private part, touching a woman, blood that does not flow, vomit that does not fill the mouth, and dozing while sitting firmly do not break wudu.

checks.q: Which breaks wudu in the Hanafi school?
w: A spot of blood that does not flow

checks.q: Which kind of sleep breaks wudu?
checks.a: Sleep without being seated firmly on the ground
w: Sleeping in the sunnah way in prostration
A moment of drowsiness while sitting

checks.q: Laughing out loud during the prayer…
checks.a: Breaks both the prayer and the wudu

cards.x: Ghusl becomes fard after the release of semen with desire, after intercourse even without release, and when menstruation or post-natal bleeding ends.
Rinse the whole mouth, wash inside the nose, and wash the whole body once, so that no dry spot remains, including the navel and under the beard.
A man must wet the inside of his plaited hair. A woman does not have to undo her plaits if water reaches the roots.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, rinsing the mouth in ghusl is…
Which makes ghusl fard?
Must a woman undo her plaits for ghusl?
checks.a: No, if water reaches the roots of her hair

lessons.title: Tayammum: when there is no water

cards.x: When you are a mile or more from water, when using water would make you ill or worse, when it is dangerously cold, or when you need the water to drink.
Make the intention, strike clean earth with both palms and wipe the whole face; strike again and wipe both arms including the elbows.
Tayammum stands in place of wudu and ghusl. It ends when water becomes available and you are able to use it.

checks.q: Which of these allows tayammum?
checks.a: Water is a mile or more away

checks.q: How many times are the hands struck on the earth?
checks.a: Twice: once for the face, once for the arms

checks.q: What ends tayammum, besides what breaks wudu?
checks.a: Finding water you are able to use

title: Prayer
sub: Its conditions, pillars and the mistakes that ruin it

cards.x: You must be in wudu (and ghusl if needed), and your body, clothes and the place you pray on must be clean of impurity.
Cover the 'awrah. For a man it is from the navel to below the knees. For a woman it is the whole body except the face, the hands and the feet.
Face the qiblah, pray after the time has come in, and intend the prayer you are praying, such as today's Zuhr.
Begin with 'Allahu akbar' while standing, saying it so that you hear yourself.

checks.q: What is a man's 'awrah in prayer?
checks.a: From the navel to below the knees
w: From the chest to the ankles
The whole body except the face

checks.q: If you pray before the time has come in…
w: It counts if you meant well

checks.q: Which is a condition for the prayer?

cards.x: Inside the prayer, four things are pillars: standing, reciting, bowing (ruku') and prostrating (sujud).
Sitting at the end of the prayer for as long as it takes to recite the tashahhud is also counted as a pillar by many.
If a pillar is missed, the prayer is not valid and must be prayed again. The prostration of forgetfulness cannot fix it.

checks.q: Which is a pillar of prayer?
w: Placing the right hand over the left

checks.q: If you miss a pillar…
checks.a: The prayer must be prayed again
w: Two prostrations of forgetfulness fix it

checks.q: How long is the final sitting at least?
checks.a: As long as it takes to recite the tashahhud
w: As long as the whole prayer

cards.x: Wajib acts include: reciting al-Fatihah, adding a surah or three verses, calmness in every position, the first sitting, the tashahhud, and ending with 'al-salam'.
If you leave a wajib act by mistake, make two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) at the end, with tashahhud and salam.
If you leave a wajib act deliberately, you are sinful and must repeat the prayer.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, reciting al-Fatihah is…
w: Recommended only in the first rak'ah

checks.q: You forgot the first sitting. What do you do?
checks.a: Make the two prostrations of forgetfulness at the end
w: Start the prayer again straight away

checks.q: You left a wajib act on purpose. What follows?
checks.a: You are sinful and must repeat the prayer
w: Two prostrations of forgetfulness are enough

cards.x: Speaking breaks the prayer, even by forgetfulness or mistake.
Eating or drinking anything, even a little, breaks it.
A lot of movement, or turning the chest away from the qiblah, breaks it.
Returning a greeting, or replying to someone with words such as 'al-hamdu lillah' as an answer, breaks it.

checks.q: You forgot you were praying and said a word. Is the prayer broken?
checks.a: Yes, speaking breaks it even by forgetfulness
w: Only if it was a long sentence

checks.q: Someone greets you while you pray. If you reply 'wa 'alaykum al-salam'…
w: It is fine if said quietly

checks.q: Which breaks the prayer?
checks.a: Turning the chest away from the qiblah
w: Glancing to the side without turning

cards.x: In the Hanafi school, the witr prayer is wajib.
Witr is three rak'ahs with one salam at the end, and a surah after al-Fatihah in every rak'ah.
In the third rak'ah, before bowing, say 'Allahu akbar', raise the hands and recite the qunut.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, witr is…
How many rak'ahs is witr in the Hanafi school?
When is the qunut recited in witr?
checks.a: In the third rak'ah, before bowing
w: After bowing in the second rak'ah
Only in Ramadan's last ten nights

title: Fasting
sub: Ramadan: what breaks the fast and what doesn't

lessons.title: What does not break the fast

cards.x: If you eat, drink or have intercourse having forgotten you are fasting, your fast is not broken.
Applying kohl or oil, smoke or dust entering the throat without your doing, and waking up in a state of janabah do not break the fast.
Backbiting does not break the fast, but it ruins its reward. Guard your tongue while fasting.

checks.q: You forgot you were fasting and drank water. Your fast…
w: Is broken and must be made up

checks.q: Does applying kohl break the fast?
Waking up in janabah while fasting…
w: Makes the fast disliked and void

cards.x: Deliberately eating, drinking, or having intercourse during a Ramadan fast, with no excuse and not forced, requires a make-up day and the expiation.
Fast two months in a row. If you truly cannot, feed sixty poor people two meals each, or give their value.
Some things break the fast but need only a make-up day, such as swallowing a pebble, or medicine reaching the stomach.

checks.q: Someone eats on purpose in Ramadan with no excuse. What is due?
checks.a: A make-up day and the expiation

checks.q: The expiation for breaking a Ramadan fast, for one who can fast, is…
checks.a: Fasting two months in a row

checks.q: Swallowing a small pebble while fasting requires…

cards.x: A traveller and someone who is ill may break the fast and make it up later.
A woman in menstruation or post-natal bleeding does not fast, and makes up the days later. She does not make up the prayers.
Someone too old to fast who will not become able gives a fidyah for each day instead.

checks.q: A woman misses fasts because of menstruation. She…
Who may break the fast and make it up later?
A very old person who cannot fast…
checks.a: Gives a fidyah for each day

title: Zakat
sub: Who pays, how much, and who may receive it

cards.x: Zakat is fard on a free, adult, sane Muslim who fully owns the nisab, once a full (lunar) year has passed on it.
The nisab is 200 dirhams of silver or 20 mithqals of gold, or the same value in money or trade goods.
Take away what you owe. If what remains still reaches the nisab, zakat is due on it.

checks.q: When does zakat become due on wealth?
checks.a: When a full year has passed on the nisab
w: As soon as you earn it

checks.q: What is the nisab of gold?
A person has the nisab but also debts. What happens?
checks.a: The debt is taken away first; zakat is due if the rest reaches the nisab

cards.x: Zakat on gold, silver, money and trade goods is a fortieth (2.5%).
Goods bought to sell are valued, and zakat is paid on their value.
You don't have to say 'this is zakat'. You may give it like a gift, as long as you intend it as zakat.

checks.q: What is the rate of zakat on money?
Must you tell the poor person 'this is zakat'?
w: Yes, or it does not count

checks.q: Is zakat due on goods you bought to sell?
w: Only if you sell them that year

cards.x: The poor, the needy, those who collect it, those in debt, those striving in the path of Allah, the stranded traveller, and (in its time) freeing captives.
You may not give your zakat to your parents, grandparents, children or grandchildren, nor (in Imam Abu Hanifah's view) to your spouse.
Zakat may not be given to Banu Hashim, the family of the Prophet ﷺ, even if they are poor. Help them with gifts instead.

checks.q: Can you give your zakat to your own mother?
How are poor descendants of Banu Hashim helped?
checks.a: With gifts and charity that is not zakat

checks.q: Which may receive zakat?

title: The heart
sub: Tazkiyah: sincerity, repentance and guarding yourself

cards.x: Imam al-Ghazali رحمه الله begins by asking why you seek knowledge. If it is to compete, show off and win people's attention, you are tearing down your religion. If it is for guidance, the angels spread their wings for you as you walk.
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Actions are only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended.'

checks.q: According to al-Ghazali, seeking knowledge to show off…
w: Is fine if the knowledge is true

checks.q: According to the hadith, actions are judged by…

cards.x: Repentance (tawbah) means turning back from what the Shari'ah blames to what it praises.
Regret for what you did, stopping the sin straight away, and resolving never to return to it.
If the sin wronged someone, part of repentance is giving their right back or asking their forgiveness.

checks.q: Which is a condition of repentance?
How many conditions does al-Qushayri give for repentance?
Repentance means turning…
checks.a: From what the Shari'ah blames to what it praises

cards.x: Al-Ghazali warns of the faults of the tongue, among them lying, backbiting, arguing, praising yourself and cursing.
The Prophet ﷺ described backbiting as mentioning your brother with something he would dislike. If it is true, it is backbiting; if it is false, it is slander.
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or stay silent.'

checks.q: Mentioning a brother's real fault behind his back is…
Which is one of the faults of the tongue al-Ghazali lists?

cards.x: Envy (hasad) is wanting a blessing to leave someone, even when you gain nothing from it. Al-Ghazali quotes the hadith: 'Envy eats good deeds as fire eats wood.'
Showing off (riya') is the hidden shirk: seeking a place in people's hearts through your worship. Al-Ghazali says most people are ruined by it.
Self-admiration ('ujb) is being pleased with yourself and seeing yourself better than others. It leads to pride.

checks.q: Wishing someone's blessing would leave them is…
Praying longer because people are watching is…
Seeing yourself as better than others is…

cards.x: Al-Ghazali wrote to his student: 'Knowledge without action is madness, and action without knowledge does not happen.'
Knowledge will not keep you away from sins today, nor bring you to obey, unless you act on it.
Al-Ghazali says: your moments are your life, and your life is your capital. Every breath is a jewel that cannot be replaced once it is gone.

checks.q: Al-Ghazali said knowledge without action is…
What makes knowledge benefit you?
Al-Ghazali calls your life…
